First, we recall the different forms of the secant-tangent Identity:

$$
\begin{aligned} & (1) & 1+{tan}^{2}⁡x={sec}^{2}⁡x \\  & (2) & {tan}^{2}⁡x={sec}^{2}⁡x-1 \\  & (3) & {sec}^{2}⁡x-{tan}^{2}⁡x=1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can rewrite our expression using $(2),$ as follows:

$$
\frac{{tan}^{2}⁡x}{\operatorname{sec}⁡x+1}-1=\frac{{sec}^{2}⁡x-1}{\operatorname{sec}⁡x+1}-1
$$

Finally, we can further simplify our expression by factoring the numerator as a difference of squares, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{sec}^{2}⁡x-1}{\operatorname{sec}⁡x+1}-1 & =\frac{(\operatorname{sec}⁡x+1)(\operatorname{sec}⁡x-1)}{\operatorname{sec}⁡x+1}-1 \\  & =\frac{\cancel{(\operatorname{sec}⁡x+1)}(\operatorname{sec}⁡x-1)}{\cancel{\operatorname{sec}⁡x+1}}-1 \\  & =\operatorname{sec}⁡x-1-1 \\  & =\operatorname{sec}⁡x-2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
\frac{{tan}^{2}⁡x}{\operatorname{sec}⁡x+1}-1=\operatorname{sec}⁡x-2.
$$
